quests.instruction: Arrange this introduction so the reader knows why the essay exists before meeting its claim.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about the benefits of learning to type quickly
options: Most people spend hours a day typing without ever having learned how to do it efficiently.
The following paragraphs consider speed, accuracy, and the strain it removes from daily work.
This essay looks at what changes when someone finally learns proper typing technique.
Learning to type quickly saves more time over a year than almost any other small skill a person can pick up.
quests.hint: An introduction usually earns the reader's attention before stating its purpose, and states its purpose before committing to a claim.
quests.explanation: The everyday problem gives the reader a reason to keep reading, and the purpose statement explains what the essay intends to do about it. The thesis then commits to a specific claim, and the preview closes by outlining what is coming, which only makes sense once the claim exists to preview.
quests.thesisStatement: Learning to type quickly saves more time over a year than almost any other small skill a person can pick up.

quests.instruction: Order the introduction so it establishes why the subject deserves attention before naming the essay's angle.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about the decline of handwritten letters
options: Fewer people write letters by hand than at any point in the last century.
The habit of writing letters is worth reviving, not out of nostalgia, but because it forces a kind of attention email cannot.
That shift matters because something about slow, deliberate communication gets lost when every message can be sent instantly.
This essay considers what letter-writing demanded of its writers and what modern communication has quietly given up.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that simply notices a change, the one that explains its significance, the one that commits to a position, and the one that maps the essay ahead.
quests.explanation: The observation introduces the change without yet interpreting it. Why it matters explains the stakes, which have to be established before the thesis can argue for reviving the habit. The roadmap comes last because it can only preview an essay whose claim has already been stated.
quests.thesisStatement: The habit of writing letters is worth reviving because it forces a kind of attention that instant communication does not.

quests.instruction: Sequence this introduction so a striking detail leads somewhere rather than sitting alone.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about the hidden cost of constant notifications
options: Constant notifications cost people more focus than the time spent looking at the screen would suggest.
This essay looks at what that cost actually is and what a person might do about it.
Most of those checks are triggered not by need but by a small red number demanding attention.
The average phone owner checks their device more than a hundred times a day.
quests.hint: A striking detail needs to be interpreted before it can support a claim, and a claim needs to exist before the essay can promise a direction.
quests.explanation: The striking detail earns attention through a number, and the interpretation explains what that number actually reveals. The thesis turns that interpretation into a specific claim about cost, and the direction sentence closes by pointing toward what the essay will explore, which depends on the claim already being stated.
quests.thesisStatement: Constant notifications cost people more focus than the time spent looking at the screen would suggest.

quests.instruction: Arrange the background information so the reader has enough context before the claim appears.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some countries are shifting school exams online
options: This essay weighs both sides before considering what schools should keep in mind during the shift.
Written exams have shaped how schools measure learning for well over a century.
In the last decade, a growing number of school systems have started moving some exams onto computers.
Moving exams online improves fairness in some ways while introducing new risks in others.
quests.hint: Background should move from what has long been true to what has recently changed, and only then to the essay's own claim about that change.
quests.explanation: The background fact establishes the long-standing norm the reader needs before understanding what counts as a change. The recent development names that change, which the thesis then evaluates. The scope statement closes by describing what the essay will do with that evaluation.
quests.thesisStatement: Moving exams online improves fairness in some ways while introducing new risks in others.

quests.instruction: Order this introduction so relevant background comes before the claim it supports.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why apprenticeships are regaining popularity
options: Apprenticeships deserve to be treated as equal to a university degree, not as a fallback option.
Apprenticeships once offered a common path into skilled trades before university degrees became the default expectation.
The sections that follow look at cost, employability, and the kind of learning each path actually provides.
In recent years, rising tuition costs and skills shortages have brought apprenticeships back into serious consideration.
quests.hint: Context about the past should come before a claim about the present, and the claim should exist before the essay maps its structure.
quests.explanation: The historical context explains what apprenticeships used to mean, which the shift noted then updates for the present. The thesis argues for a specific status based on that shift, and the preview outlines the essay's structure, which only makes sense once that status has been claimed.
quests.thesisStatement: Apprenticeships deserve to be treated as equal to a university degree, not as a fallback option.

quests.instruction: This introduction includes one piece of background that is easy to place wrong. Order all four sentences correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about the return of vinyl records
options: Vinyl records nearly disappeared from shops once CDs, and later streaming, took over how people listened to music.
Vinyl's revival is driven less by sound quality than by the physical ritual of choosing and playing a record.
Yet sales of new vinyl records have grown for over a decade, even among listeners too young to remember them the first time.
This essay considers what that ritual offers listeners that a streaming playlist does not.
quests.hint: The complicating detail should surprise the reader given the background, which means it has to follow the background rather than come before it.
quests.explanation: The background explains why vinyl's return is unexpected in the first place. The complicating detail, the unlikely growth in sales, only counts as surprising once the reader knows vinyl was expected to disappear. The thesis interprets that surprise, and the direction sentence closes the introduction.
quests.thesisStatement: Vinyl's revival is driven less by sound quality than by the physical ritual of choosing and playing a record.

quests.instruction: Arrange this introduction so it narrows smoothly from a wide observation to a precise claim.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some students thrive under pressure while others do not
options: Pressure affects every student differently, and reactions to a looming deadline can look almost nothing alike.
Students perform better under pressure when they believe their effort, not luck, decides the result.
This essay examines what builds that sense of control and how it can be encouraged in a classroom.
Look closely, though, and the difference often comes down to how much control a student feels they have over the outcome.
quests.hint: Each sentence should narrow the field of possible essays. By the end, only one claim should still be standing.
quests.explanation: The wide observation opens with a statement broad enough to fit any student. The narrower pattern identifies one specific factor within that wide field, which the thesis then turns into a precise, arguable claim. The preview closes by outlining what the essay will explore.
quests.thesisStatement: Students perform better under pressure when they believe their effort, not luck, decides the result.

quests.instruction: Order the introduction from a general truth to the essay's exact angle on it.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some workplace meetings feel like a waste of time
options: This essay focuses on how a short agenda line can make that shift possible.
Many of the ones that feel wasted share one trait: nobody agreed beforehand on what decision the meeting needed to make.
Meetings are a fixture of almost every modern workplace.
Meetings become worthwhile the moment they are built around a single decision rather than a general update.
quests.hint: Track the narrowing: an institution everyone recognises, a pattern within it, a claim about that pattern, and finally the essay's exact focus.
quests.explanation: The general truth about meetings is too broad to argue with, so it opens. The specific pattern narrows that truth to one shared trait among wasted meetings, and the thesis converts that pattern into a claim about what fixes it. The scope sentence names the essay's exact focus, which depends on the claim already existing.
quests.thesisStatement: Meetings become worthwhile the moment they are built around a single decision rather than a general update.

quests.instruction: Move this introduction from a wide claim about human behaviour down to one precise, testable idea.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why people procrastinate on tasks they actually enjoy
options: This essay explores that fear of imperfect beginnings and what loosens its grip.
People are often assumed to procrastinate only on tasks they dislike.
People procrastinate on enjoyable tasks when the task feels too important to start imperfectly.
Yet many people delay tasks they genuinely look forward to, from a favourite hobby to a long-planned trip.
quests.hint: The surprising narrowing should complicate the wide claim before the thesis resolves that complication with a specific explanation.
quests.explanation: The wide claim states the common assumption, and the surprising narrowing complicates it with a counterexample the reader has to account for. The thesis resolves that tension with a specific explanation, and the preview closes by pointing toward the rest of the essay.
quests.thesisStatement: People procrastinate on enjoyable tasks when the task feels too important to start imperfectly.

quests.instruction: Two sentences could plausibly serve as the thesis. Choose correctly and order the paragraph.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about whether group projects prepare students for real teamwork
options: This essay looks at what changes when a teacher grades collaboration itself rather than the finished product alone.
In practice, group projects teach real teamwork only when the grading rewards the process, not just the final result.
School group projects are often defended as preparation for teamwork later in life.
In theory, dividing a task among several people should build exactly the collaboration skills a workplace needs.
quests.hint: One sentence states an ideal in theory; the other commits to a specific condition. The one that could be argued against is the real thesis.
quests.explanation: The context explains why group projects are assigned at all. The almost-thesis restates the ideal without committing to a condition, which is why the actual thesis, with its specific condition about grading, has to follow it rather than replace it. The preview closes once the real claim is in place.
quests.thesisStatement: Group projects teach real teamwork only when the grading rewards the collaborative process, not just the final result.

quests.instruction: Place the thesis where it belongs, after enough context, rather than too early or too late.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some companies are shortening the traditional work week
options: A growing number of companies are now experimenting with four-day schedules instead.
For most of the last century, a five-day work week has been treated as an unquestioned standard.
This essay looks at what those cut tasks tend to be and why removing them rarely hurts output.
A shorter work week can raise productivity, not just employee satisfaction, when it forces teams to cut low-value tasks.
quests.hint: The thesis needs the trend to already be named before it can make a claim about that trend's effect.
quests.explanation: The context establishes the old standard. The trend noted names the recent change, which the thesis then makes a specific claim about, that the shift raises productivity through cutting low-value work. The roadmap closes the introduction, previewing content that depends on the thesis existing.
quests.thesisStatement: A shorter work week can raise productivity, not just employee satisfaction, when it forces teams to cut low-value tasks.

quests.instruction: This introduction buries its thesis in the middle. Reorder it so the claim sits where a reader expects to find it.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about whether online reviews should be independently verified
options: Online platforms should verify a purchase before allowing a review to be posted.
This essay considers how such a system might work without discouraging honest feedback.
Yet many of those reviews are written by people who never actually bought the product, which undermines their value.
Shoppers increasingly decide what to buy based on reviews left by previous customers.
quests.hint: The problem must be established before the thesis proposes a fix for it, and the fix must exist before the essay can preview how it would work.
quests.explanation: The background introduces the habit of relying on reviews. The problem raised explains what undermines that habit, which the thesis then answers with a specific proposal. The preview closes by describing what the essay will explore about implementing that proposal.
quests.thesisStatement: Online platforms should verify a purchase before allowing a review to be posted.

quests.instruction: One opening sentence risks pulling the essay off-topic. Order the introduction so it stays anchored to the real subject.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why public speaking anxiety can be reduced through practice
options: This essay looks at how targeted practice differs from simply rehearsing a whole speech.
Public speaking anxiety fades fastest when a speaker practises the specific moments they fear most, such as the opening line.
That nervousness usually comes from uncertainty about what will happen next, not from the audience itself.
Few situations make people as visibly nervous as standing in front of an audience.
quests.hint: Avoid an opening that wanders into a related but separate topic, such as public speaking in general history. Stay on anxiety and what reduces it.
quests.explanation: The focused opening stays tightly on nervousness rather than drifting into a broader history of public speaking. The relevant detail narrows the cause of that nervousness, and the thesis proposes a targeted fix based on that cause. The preview closes by pointing to how the essay will explore that fix.
quests.thesisStatement: Public speaking anxiety fades fastest when a speaker practises the specific moments they fear most.

quests.instruction: Order the introduction so a tempting but tangential fact is placed correctly rather than derailing the opening.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why recipe blogs often include long personal stories before the recipe itself
options: Many readers scroll past paragraphs of a blogger's life story just to find the ingredient list they came for.
That long introduction usually exists because search engines favour pages with more original written content, not fewer.
Recipe blogs are shaped more by search engine rules than by any writer's storytelling instinct.
This essay looks at how those rules quietly shape a format readers often find frustrating.
quests.hint: The reason behind the frustration could easily wander into an unrelated discussion of search engines in general. Keep it tied to why recipe blogs specifically look this way.
quests.explanation: The reader frustration opens with a shared, recognisable experience. The reason behind it stays tied to that experience rather than drifting into search engines generally, and the thesis turns that reason into a claim about what shapes the format. The preview closes the introduction.
quests.thesisStatement: Recipe blogs are shaped more by search engine rules than by any writer's storytelling instinct.

quests.instruction: Reorder this introduction so it resists the temptation to open with an unrelated statistic.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why board games are experiencing a resurgence among adults
options: Board games were once treated as something families packed away once children grew out of them.
In the last several years, adult-focused board game cafés and design studios have multiplied in most major cities.
This essay considers what that focused time offers that other forms of socialising increasingly do not.
Board games appeal to adults now because they offer focused social time that a phone cannot interrupt.
quests.hint: An opening about screen time in general could easily hijack this essay. Keep the focus on board games and what specifically draws adults back to them.
quests.explanation: The on-topic opening stays with board games rather than opening on the broader subject of screen time. The relevant shift narrows to a recent, specific change, and the thesis explains the reason behind that shift. The preview closes by pointing toward the essay's focus.
quests.thesisStatement: Board games appeal to adults now because they offer focused social time that a phone cannot interrupt.

quests.instruction: Arrange this introduction so a cause is established before its effect is claimed.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some students lose interest in reading during their teenage years
options: This essay considers what changes when teenagers are given more say over what they read.
Many children who loved reading at ten years old rarely pick up a book by the time they turn sixteen.
Around that age, assigned reading tends to replace reading chosen freely, and the two feel very different to a teenager.
Teenagers lose interest in reading less because of the books themselves than because of who is choosing them.
quests.hint: The thesis makes a claim about a cause. That cause needs to be identified in an earlier sentence before the thesis can assert it as the explanation.
quests.explanation: The observation states the pattern needing explanation. The cause identified names a specific change around that age, which the thesis then asserts as the real explanation. The preview closes by pointing to the essay's proposed remedy.
quests.thesisStatement: Teenagers lose interest in reading less because of the books themselves than because of who is choosing them.

quests.instruction: Order this introduction so the reader understands the effect only after the cause has been named.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why open-plan classrooms have fallen out of favour
options: Open-plan classrooms fell out of favour because they underestimated how much students rely on a quiet, defined space to focus.
Teachers eventually found that noise from one group made it difficult for another to concentrate nearby.
Open-plan classrooms, with few or no walls between groups, were popular in school design decades ago.
This essay looks at what modern classroom design has learned from that earlier experiment.
quests.hint: The thesis explains why a trend reversed. The reason for that reversal has to be introduced before the thesis can claim it as the explanation.
quests.explanation: The historical note introduces the trend being explained. The cause of change identifies the specific difficulty that emerged, which the thesis then names directly as the reason the trend reversed. The preview closes the introduction by pointing to what came after.
quests.thesisStatement: Open-plan classrooms fell out of favour because they underestimated how much students rely on a quiet space to focus.

quests.instruction: Sequence this introduction so the reader can see the effect grow logically from its stated cause.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why customer complaints often increase after a company launches a new app
options: This essay looks at how companies can distinguish real problems from ordinary adjustment friction.
Companies often see a spike in complaints in the weeks right after launching a new app, even when the app works well.
A temporary rise in complaints usually reflects unfamiliarity with a new layout rather than a genuine decline in quality.
Much of that spike comes from customers who simply have not yet learned where familiar features moved to.
quests.hint: The pattern needs an explanation before the thesis can reinterpret it. Place the underlying cause where it can do that work.
quests.explanation: The pattern noticed states the surprising fact that needs explaining. The underlying cause supplies that explanation, which the thesis then uses to reinterpret the pattern as something other than a quality problem. The preview closes the introduction.
quests.thesisStatement: A temporary rise in complaints usually reflects unfamiliarity with a new layout rather than a genuine decline in quality.

quests.instruction: The link between the opening and the thesis is less obvious here. Trace it and order the introduction.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some museums have started allowing visitors to touch certain exhibits
options: Allowing visitors to touch selected, durable exhibits deepens engagement without meaningfully risking the collection.
This essay considers which kinds of objects can safely bear that kind of contact.
Museums have traditionally protected their collections by keeping visitors at a careful distance.
That distance, though respectful, can leave visitors feeling like observers of history rather than participants in it.
quests.hint: The bridge sentence connects a tradition to a cost of that tradition. Find it before assuming the thesis follows directly from the opening.
quests.explanation: The distant starting point describes a long-standing norm that, on its own, does not obviously lead anywhere. The bridge sentence supplies the missing link by naming a downside of that norm, which the thesis then answers with a specific proposal. The preview closes the introduction.
quests.thesisStatement: Allowing visitors to touch selected, durable exhibits deepens engagement without meaningfully risking the collection.

quests.instruction: This introduction requires an inferential leap the reader needs help with. Place the bridging sentence correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some restaurants have removed prices from their menus for tasting courses
options: Removing that price for a fixed tasting course shifts a diner's attention from cost to the meal as a single experience.
Pricing a tasting menu as one experience, rather than itemising each course, changes how diners judge its value.
A menu traditionally lists a price beside every dish so a diner can plan a meal in advance.
This essay looks at what diners gain and lose when a meal is priced this way.
quests.hint: Without the bridge, the jump from listing prices to a claim about value judgement would feel sudden. Find the sentence that explains the shift.
quests.explanation: The distant starting point describes an ordinary, expected practice. The bridge explains what changes psychologically when that practice is altered, which prepares the reader for the thesis's specific claim about value judgement. The preview closes the introduction.
quests.thesisStatement: Pricing a tasting menu as one experience, rather than itemising each course, changes how diners judge its value.

quests.instruction: Order this introduction so the reader can follow an indirect connection between two ideas that do not obviously belong together at first.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some software companies have started removing user ratings from their apps
options: Removing star ratings in favour of written feedback gives users a more accurate sense of an app's real strengths and weaknesses.
A single low rating, though, can carry the same visual weight as hundreds of positive ones, distorting what the average actually represents.
This essay examines what companies risk losing along with the ratings they remove.
Star ratings have shaped how people choose an app for over a decade.
quests.hint: The bridge should explain a flaw hidden inside the starting point before the thesis proposes an alternative to that flaw.
quests.explanation: The distant starting point describes a familiar system without hinting at any problem yet. The bridge reveals the hidden flaw in that system, which the thesis then answers with a proposed alternative. The preview closes by pointing to a remaining cost of that alternative.
quests.thesisStatement: Removing star ratings in favour of written feedback gives users a more accurate sense of an app's strengths and weaknesses.

quests.instruction: One sentence in this introduction is written for the conclusion, not the opening. Reorder it correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some universities are removing standardised test scores from admissions
options: A growing number of universities have stopped requiring that score altogether.
This essay considers what universities use instead and whether it succeeds in being fairer.
For decades, a single test score has carried enormous weight in university admissions decisions.
Removing standardised test scores lets admissions officers see a fuller, fairer picture of each applicant.
quests.hint: Check that no sentence here is quietly trying to summarise the whole essay before it has even started.
quests.explanation: The context introduces the traditional weight given to test scores, and the trend names the recent shift away from that practice. The thesis claims a specific benefit of that shift, and the preview, rather than summarising conclusions, simply points to what the essay will examine next.
quests.thesisStatement: Removing standardised test scores lets admissions officers see a fuller, fairer picture of each applicant.

quests.instruction: This introduction has its thesis placed too early, before the context that justifies it. Fix the order.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some airlines have redesigned economy seating around personal space rather than legroom
options: Airlines have spent years advertising extra legroom as the main upgrade passengers want.
This essay looks at what such a redesign would require airlines to change.
Redesigning economy seating around personal space would address the discomfort passengers actually report most.
Passenger surveys, however, consistently rank shoulder space and armrest access above legroom as sources of daily discomfort.
quests.hint: A thesis placed before its justifying context asks the reader to accept a claim before knowing why it matters. Find where the claim truly belongs.
quests.explanation: The context establishes the assumption airlines have acted on. The complication challenges that assumption with survey evidence, which the thesis then uses to propose a different priority. The preview closes by pointing to the practical implications of that priority.
quests.thesisStatement: Redesigning economy seating around personal space would address the discomfort passengers actually report most.

quests.instruction: This introduction mixes up its context and its preview. Restore the logical order.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some cities are replacing traffic lights with roundabouts at busy intersections
options: This essay looks at why that trade-off, fewer serious crashes for more minor ones, is one cities should accept.
Studies of intersections converted to roundabouts show fewer serious collisions, even though minor fender-benders sometimes rise slightly.
Roundabouts make busy intersections safer overall, even if they feel less predictable to drivers used to lights.
Traffic lights have controlled busy intersections in most cities for well over a century.
quests.hint: The evidence needs to appear before the thesis interprets it, and the preview needs the thesis to exist before it can point ahead.
quests.explanation: The context introduces the long-standing default option. The evidence of problem presents specific findings, which the thesis then interprets as an overall safety claim. The preview closes by pointing to the trade-off the essay will defend.
quests.thesisStatement: Roundabouts make busy intersections safer overall, even if they feel less predictable to drivers used to lights.

quests.instruction: Two openings both sound reasonable. Choose the one that actually sets up this specific thesis, then order the paragraph.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why mentorship programmes often fail within their first year
options: Most failures trace back to mentors and mentees being paired without any shared goal beyond general encouragement.
Mentorship programmes succeed when pairs are matched around a specific, shared objective rather than general encouragement.
This essay looks at how programmes can build that kind of matching from the start.
Many mentorship programmes are launched with enthusiasm and quietly abandoned within a year.
quests.hint: An opening about mentorship's popularity in general would not connect as tightly to this specific thesis about failure and matching. Choose the one that does.
quests.explanation: The chosen opening focuses on the exact pattern the essay will explain, not mentorship in general. The specific detail narrows the cause of that pattern, and the thesis proposes a fix aimed precisely at that cause. The preview closes the introduction.
quests.thesisStatement: Mentorship programmes succeed when pairs are matched around a specific, shared objective rather than general encouragement.

quests.instruction: Decide which of two plausible-looking sentences actually belongs as context here, and place all four correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some restaurants have started charging a fee for reservations that are not honoured
options: Restaurants that hold a table for a booking receive no compensation if the diners simply never arrive.
A missed reservation on a busy night can cost a small restaurant hundreds of pounds in lost revenue.
This essay considers how such a fee could be designed to feel reasonable rather than punitive.
Charging a fee for unhonoured reservations is a fair way to protect restaurants without discouraging honest bookings.
quests.hint: One possible opening would drift into restaurant pricing generally; the relevant context here stays tied to the specific problem of no-shows.
quests.explanation: The relevant context introduces the specific problem, not restaurant economics broadly. The consequence named quantifies that problem, which the thesis then answers with a proposed policy. The preview closes by pointing to how that policy could be designed fairly.
quests.thesisStatement: Charging a fee for unhonoured reservations is a fair way to protect restaurants without discouraging honest bookings.

quests.instruction: Between a dramatic opening and a measured one, choose the one that fits this essay's tone, then order the introduction.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay evaluating whether remote job interviews disadvantage some candidates
options: Remote interviews have become common enough that many candidates now expect them as the default.
This essay looks at what employers could do to make remote interviews fairer for every applicant.
Remote interviews can disadvantage capable candidates for reasons that have nothing to do with their qualifications.
Not every candidate, though, has access to a quiet room, reliable internet, or a professional-looking background at home.
quests.hint: A measured opening suits an evaluative essay better than a dramatic one. Check that the specific concern narrows toward the actual thesis rather than away from it.
quests.explanation: The measured opening establishes the now-common practice without exaggeration. The specific concern narrows to the exact disadvantage the essay will examine, and the thesis states that disadvantage as a claim. The preview closes by pointing toward possible solutions.
quests.thesisStatement: Remote interviews can disadvantage capable candidates for reasons that have nothing to do with their qualifications.

quests.instruction: Build a complete, polished introduction: an anchored opening, a bridge, a precise thesis, and a preview that only works once the thesis exists.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some workplaces have started discouraging after-hours email
options: That habit blurs the line between being available and never actually being off duty.
Many employees now check work email during evenings and weekends without ever being asked to.
Discouraging after-hours email protects employee wellbeing without meaningfully slowing down the work itself.
This essay looks at how companies have implemented that boundary and what happened afterward.
quests.hint: Check each sentence against everything this file has covered: does it earn attention, connect ideas, commit to a claim, and preview only what the claim allows?
quests.explanation: The anchored opening stays tightly on the specific habit rather than email in general. The bridge names the cost of that habit, preparing the reader for the thesis, which claims a specific benefit to restricting it. The preview closes by pointing to real-world evidence the essay will use.
quests.thesisStatement: Discouraging after-hours email protects employee wellbeing without meaningfully slowing down the work itself.

quests.instruction: This introduction tests distance between ideas: place an indirect bridge and a precise thesis correctly among the four sentences.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some parks have started planting more native, low-maintenance plants instead of decorative flower beds
options: Keeping those beds colourful, though, usually requires steady watering and replanting that a warming climate makes harder to justify.
This essay considers what a park loses in colour and what it gains in resilience.
Native, low-maintenance planting serves a park's purpose better than decorative beds that demand resources the climate can no longer spare easily.
Public parks have long been judged partly by how colourful their flower beds look each season.
quests.hint: The bridge should connect an aesthetic standard to a practical cost before the thesis argues for changing that standard.
quests.explanation: The distant opening states a familiar aesthetic expectation. The bridge exposes the practical cost hidden inside that expectation, which the thesis then weighs against a different approach. The preview closes by naming the trade-off honestly.
quests.thesisStatement: Native, low-maintenance planting serves a park's purpose better than decorative beds that demand resources the climate can no longer spare.

quests.instruction: Full integration: order this introduction using everything from narrowing to thesis placement to a preview that depends on the claim.
quests.essayTopic: Introduce an essay about why some schools have replaced detention with structured reflection conversations
options: A short, structured conversation about the behaviour's impact changes a student's future choices more reliably than detention alone.
Schools have used detention as a standard consequence for misbehaviour for generations.
Detention on its own rarely explains to a student why their behaviour caused a problem in the first place.
This essay looks at how schools have trained staff to hold these conversations well.
quests.hint: Move from what has long been standard, to what that standard fails to do, to a precise claim about a better approach, to a preview grounded in that claim.
quests.explanation: The broad context introduces the long-standing practice. The narrowed problem identifies its specific shortcoming, which the thesis answers with a precise alternative claim. The preview closes by pointing to how that alternative has actually been carried out.
quests.thesisStatement: A short, structured conversation about a behaviour's impact changes a student's future choices more reliably than detention alone.
